topics.title: 👋 Welcome — the 3-step idea
topics.text: Every PollSlide presentation works the same way, whether it's a poll, survey, quiz, or study set. 1 · Build Create a presentation and add questions — type them yourself or let AI draft them for you. 2 · Stamp your slide Each question has a QR code. Drop it on your Keynote, PowerPoint, or a PDF. 3 · Go live Present. Your audience scans the QR, answers, and results animate in real time. ▶ Your first quiz in 2 minutes: create it, let Polly write the rest, add GIFs and go live. Chapters and the written steps are on the getting-started page.

topics.title: 🗳️ Create your first poll
topics.text: From a blank account to a ready question in under a minute. Sign in at app.pollslide.com . Pick a product tab — for this example, 🗳️ Polls . Click + New Poll . A fresh presentation is created. Give it a name (e.g. "Team Trivia Night") and save. You're ready to add questions — see below. Tip: On the Free plan you can keep 3 presentations. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited polls, surveys, quizzes, and study sets.

topics.title: ➕ Add a question
topics.text: Click + Add Question . Type your question in the question box . Fill in the answer options (A, B, C, D…). Choose a question type — single choice, multi-select, rating, word cloud, or free text. Mark the correct answer (for quizzes) by tapping the ✓ next to an option. In a hurry? Click ✨ Ask Polly and give it a topic or paste your notes — Polly drafts a full set of questions for you to edit.

topics.title: ↕️ Move questions within a deck
topics.text: Put your questions in the order you want to ask them. Each question keeps its QR code and link when you move it. Click the question in the list on the left. Click “✏️ Edit this question”. At the bottom of the editor, click “↑ Up” or “↓ Down”. Each click moves it one place, and the list updates straight away. What happens when you move a question Its QR code and link still open the same question. That includes QR codes on your Keynote, PowerPoint and Google Slides slides, printed handouts, and the Mac companion. You don't need to copy anything again. Its number changes to match its new place. The question list, your audience's phones and your reports number questions by where they are in the deck now. A question you move from 2nd to 5th shows as “Question 5”, even if your slide still says “Question 2”. Answers stay with their question. Results, reports, leaderboards and exports are not affected. You can move questions during a live session. If you move the question that is showing, your audience stays on it and keeps what they have chosen. Deleting a question doesn't change the other questions' codes. Anyone who scans a deleted question's code is told it isn't available, then…

topics.title: ✨ Draft it with Polly AI
topics.text: Polly is PollSlide's built-in AI. Give it a topic — or paste your notes, an outline, or a paragraph — and it writes a whole set of questions in seconds. It works for every product: polls, surveys, quizzes and study sets. Click ✨ Ask Polly on any presentation, or ✨ New with Polly to start a brand-new one from scratch. Type what you want — e.g. "5 trivia questions about the solar system" — or paste your own notes to turn into questions. Pick how many questions ( 1–30 ) and, for images, a style . Polly drafts the questions, options, and correct answers. Edit anything before you go live. 🗳️ Any product Polly matches what you're building — opinion polls, multi-question surveys, graded quizzes with correct answers, or flashcard study sets. ⚡ Fast & private Polly runs on PollSlide's own servers first for speed, with a cloud fallback. Your prompts are used only to draft your questions. Fair-use limits: Polly is metered per month by plan (Free includes a monthly allowance; Pro and Team include much more). If you hit the limit, you can still build questions by hand, or upgrade for more. See Plans & billing .

topics.title: 🖼️ Add an image with AI
topics.text: Open a question and find the image row. Click ✨ Generate with AI — PollSlide creates an image from your question text. Pick a style (Illustration, Realistic, 3D, Cartoon, Minimal, Watercolor). Prefer your own? Click ⬆ Upload or paste an image / GIF / video URL. Use the S / M / L / ⛶ buttons to size the media on the slide.

topics.title: ⛶ Present
topics.text: Present mode shows your question full-screen with a QR code your audience scans to answer. Click ⛶ Present on any question. Your audience points their phone camera at the QR code — no app needed. Watch responses roll in live. Switch chart styles anytime. Use 📋 Copy QR box for slide to paste the QR straight onto your own Keynote / PowerPoint / any deck. 📱 No phone to scan the QR? No problem. Anyone on a laptop (or any browser) can join without scanning: they go to pollslide.com/join and type the code shown next to your QR. Same session, same live results. So your audience always has both options, add this line under the QR on your slide : 📱 Scan the QR — or go to pollslide.com/join and enter code ABC123 In the app, the Share / QR window has a “Copy this line” button that fills in your real code for you.

topics.title: 🔗 Share without presenting
topics.text: Not every project is presented live. Surveys, quizzes and study sets can be sent out and answered at your audience's own pace — no QR on a slide required. Open your presentation and click 🔗 Share . Copy the join link (or its QR code ) and post it anywhere — a chat, an LMS, a slide, a printout. Or click ✉️ Email it to send the link straight to a list of recipients. Prefer a code? Anyone can go to pollslide.com/join and type the 6-character code . 📋 Surveys Collect feedback over hours or days. Every response flows into the same live results and CSV export. 📚 Study sets Learners review flashcards on their own with spaced repetition — share the link and they practice anytime. One link, one tally: whether people scan a QR live, join by code on a laptop, or open an emailed link, they all land in the same session — your results stay in one place.

topics.title: 📊 Post-reveal & results
topics.text: When you reveal the answer, PollSlide celebrates with leaderboards, podiums, insight chips, and confetti. In the editor, choose a post-reveal style: Leaderboard , Podium , Scorecard , or an Explainer / Did-you-know card . Set how long after the first answer to auto-reveal (or reveal manually). Add optional explainer text shown after the reveal. Turn on auto-advance to flow to the next question hands-free.

topics.title: 🎉 Reveal live
topics.text: Click Reveal now (or let the timer auto-reveal). The correct answer highlights in green ; results lock. The leaderboard / podium appears with names and response times. Advance to the next question and keep the momentum going.

topics.title: 📊 Results, reports & export
topics.text: Every response is saved. Review results live during your talk, or come back to them any time afterward — and take the raw data with you. During a session, watch results update live — bars, donuts, word clouds, leaderboards and podiums. Open 📊 Report on any presentation for the full Response Report : totals, per-question breakdowns, and per-participant answers. Click ⬇ CSV to export everything to a spreadsheet — great for grading, analysis, or your records. Running the same quiz more than once? Every reset is saved with its date , so past sessions never disappear. 🖥️ Big screen Click 🖥️ Big screen to open a clean, full-screen results view for a projector or second monitor — no companion app needed. 🔒 Your data Exports are yours to keep. Delete a session or your whole account any time — see Your data & privacy .

topics.title: ✨ AI Insights — read the room
topics.text: When your audience answers an open-text question, Polly can read every response and show you the themes, the mood, and a one-line summary — instantly, on your results panel. Perfect for "What's on your mind?", "One word for today", or any free-form question. Run any open text or word cloud question and let answers roll in — you need at least 2 . On your live results panel, click ✨ AI Insights . Polly returns a summary , an overall sentiment bar (positive / neutral / negative), and the top themes — each with a count and a real example quote. Click it again any time to re-analyze as more answers arrive. 🧠 Themes, not noise Hundreds of replies become a ranked list of what people actually said — grouped, counted, with an example each. 🔒 Private & included Polly analyzes on PollSlide's own servers first — not shipped to a third-party AI cloud — and it's included in your plan. 📊 Works in your Report too The same ✨ AI Insights button sits on every open-text question in your Report — so you can analyze feedback and survey answers long after the session ends. Tip: AI Insights shines on open-ended questions. For multiple-choice, your live bars and the Report already show the full…

Click 📚 Study this deck and PollSlide turns every question into a flashcard (question on the front, correct answer on the back). You land on your study home : your streak, how many cards are due, and a mastery bar. Pick how you want to study today — then just keep coming back. topics.text: When you hit Present, PollSlide asks how you want to run it. Classic works exactly as it always has. Everyone's phone shows what's at stake, and the big screen calls out the drama as each answer is revealed. You can switch modes between rounds — start Classic, finish on Survival for a grand finale. 🎯 Classic One point per correct answer, you reveal when you're ready. Exactly how PollSlide has always worked — nothing changes. Best for: any audience. ⚡ Speed round The faster you answer correctly, the more you score — up to double points for the quickest. The reveal crowns a Fastest Finger . Best for: parties and lifting a flat room. 🔥 Streak Correct answers in a row build a multiplier up to 3×, with flames that grow as you go. One miss resets it. topics.title: 🎪 Waiting-room warm-up
topics.text: Instead of a static "waiting for the presenter" screen while people trickle in, the big screen can run light-hearted trivia — so the room is entertained (and looking at your join code) before you've even started. Open the 🖥️ Big screen view from the top bar (that's the projector view with the join code and QR). Warm-up trivia appears automatically underneath the join banner while you're waiting. Questions rotate on their own — each shows for a few seconds, reveals its answer, then moves on. It disappears the instant you launch your first real question. Don't want it? Click 🎪 Warm-up: On in the bottom corner to switch it off — that screen remembers your choice. 🚫 No spoilers Warm-up questions come from a built-in general-knowledge set — never from your deck — so nothing in your actual quiz is given away. 👀 Keeps the code on screen The join link, code and QR stay visible above the trivia, so latecomers can still get in while everyone else plays along. ⚡ Zero setup Nothing to configure and no AI needed — it works even if your internet or AI service is having a bad day.

topics.title: 🎯 Polly Live Co-pilot
topics.text: Mid-session, Polly can read how your audience just answered and suggest a follow-up question that responds to it — which you can put on screen with one click. It's like having a co-host who noticed the room split 60/40 and knows what to ask next. Launch a question and let a few answers come in (you need at least 3 ). On your live results panel, click 🎯 Suggest a follow-up . Polly reads the actual responses and offers 3 ready-made questions , each with four options, the correct answer marked where there is one, and a short note on why it's suggesting that one. Pick one: ⚡ Add & launch now puts it live immediately, or ＋ Add to deck saves it for later. Not useful? Close it. Nothing is added or launched unless you choose it. 🧭 You're always in control Polly never launches anything by itself. Every suggestion is a proposal you accept, edit later, or ignore. 🔒 Private & included Like AI Insights, this runs on PollSlide's own AI first rather than a third-party cloud, and it's included in your plan — not charged per use. 🛟 Never blocks your session If the AI can't be reached, you get a calm "unavailable right now" message. topics.text: When a session ends, build a recap page in one click and send the link to everyone who took part — the winner, the question that fooled the room, and the highlights. Great for "same time next week?" and it works long after the session is over. Open 📊 Report from the top bar. In the filters, choose the presentation you want to recap (one at a time — that's what the recap covers). Click 🎁 Share recap . You get a link — Copy link to send it round, or Open recap to see it first. Anyone with the link can open it. No sign-in, no app, works on any phone. 🏆 The bits people care about Winner (or winning team), leaderboard, how many took part, the toughest question, and a question-by-question breakdown. ✨ With a summary when it fits If your session had written answers, Polly adds a one-line "in a nutshell" summary. If the AI isn't available, the recap still publishes with every stat intact. 🔗 Link-only, and yours to delete The page is only reachable by its unguessable link — it isn't listed or searchable. Folders group a whole lesson together — whatever mix of products it contains — and search looks inside your questions, not just their titles. In the left panel, the ribbon under the product tabs shows where you are: 📁 All › Biology 101 › Unit 3 . Every step is clickable. Click 📁 New folder at the bottom to create one. Folders go two levels deep — enough for Course › Unit without ever getting lost. To file something, open a deck's ⋯ menu and choose Move to folder… — or tick several with ☑ and move them all at once. Anything you create while inside a folder is filed there automatically. The All tab shows every product together. The Poll / Survey / Quiz / Study tabs now filter whatever folder you're in, rather than sending you to a separate screen. 🔍 Search finds questions, not just names Type a word from inside a question and it finds the deck — from any folder, and it tells you which one it's in. Open the deck's ⋯ menu in the left panel and choose 📤 Share with someone… Type their email address and add a note if it needs context. Click 📤 Send copy . They get an email, and the share appears in their PollSlide under 📥 Shared with me . When they accept, a copy lands in their library. They can rewrite every question and run it with their own audience. topics.text: Every other view answers "what happened in this session". This one answers the question you actually have: is this student getting it? Open Reports and choose Progress over time . Each student gets a row: how many sittings, their average, their best, their most recent, and a small line showing the shape of it. Worth a look at the top lists who to check on — not a ranking of your own class. Hover any row to see the reasoning behind its trend. ⏳ Two quizzes is not a trend Below three sittings it says not enough yet rather than guessing a direction. topics.title: 📶 Answers survive bad wifi
topics.text: Thirty phones on school wifi is the most ordinary thing in the world, and it used to be the one thing that could lose an answer. It can't now. A student taps Submit and the connection is down. Their phone says: "No connection — your answer is saved and will send automatically." It sends itself the moment the connection returns — even if they closed the tab and came back. They see "✓ Sent" when it lands. ⏱ The time that counts is when they tapped Not when it arrived. A student is never marked down for the school's network. The delay is recorded separately so you can see what happened. 👀 You can see which ones were late An answer that was stuck shows as sent late in your report and in the CSV, with how long it waited. You judge it; the software doesn't decide for you. 🔔 If it truly fails, nobody is left guessing After repeated attempts the student is told to tell you, and it's recorded on our side too. An answer is never dropped in silence. Nothing to switch on. This is how answering works now, on every product and every plan.

topics.title: 🎤 Atmosphere — how the wait feels
topics.text: Between launching a question and revealing the answer there's a gap, and what fills it should depend on the room. A quiz night and a board meeting want opposite things, so you pick. Press ▶ Present . The dialog that asks how you want to run it now has an Atmosphere row. Choose 🌿 Calm , 🎓 Classroom or 🎤 Game show . Press ▶ Start presenting . Your choice is remembered for that deck. 🌿 Calm No sound, no clock drama — the results simply appear. Board meetings, webinars, libraries, anywhere a noise would be rude. This is the default. 🎓 Classroom You hear the room answering and the last five seconds are unmissable, but nothing ticks at you. Suits most lessons and training. 🎤 Game show A ticking clock that speeds up as it runs out, answers landing audibly, and a held beat before the reveal. Quiz nights, conferences, a finale. It changes nothing about the quiz. Same questions, same scoring, same reveal, same results — only how the waiting feels. It's separate from game modes, so you can run Survival calmly or a Classic poll like a game show. Muting your device always wins. If you've pressed 🔇 , a deck set to Game show stays silent — a setting you chose last week can't override the…

topics.title: 👥 Class lists — one record per student
topics.text: Give a class its list of students once, and every deck you assign to it records who answered by person — not by whatever they typed that day. Open a deck's ⋯ menu and choose 👥 Assign to a class… , then ＋ New class . Give it a name — “Biology 101, Period 3” — and paste your list. One name per line, or paste a column straight out of a spreadsheet. Press Save . You'll see exactly who was added. Back in the class list, press Assign to attach this deck to that class. Students now pick their name from a list instead of typing it. 📋 Paste it however you have it Ruiz, Ana is turned into Ana Ruiz . A header row like Student Name is ignored rather than becoming a student. The same person listed twice becomes one. Extra columns — email, year group — are left alone. 🔗 The record follows the student Not the phone. Answer two questions on the school Chromebook and finish on your own phone and it's still one student with one score. Clear the browser, use a different device, spell your name differently — the record holds. 🚪 Leaving isn't deleting Re-paste an updated list and anyone no longer on it is marked as having left, never erased — their earlier work stays attached to them. topics.title: 🔐 Making sure it's really them
topics.text: A list of names lets a student pick their own — and, without something more, lets them pick somebody else's. Choose how your class proves who they are. Open 👥 Assign to a class… → Students on the class you want. Pick one of the three methods below. The class starts on PIN . Students are asked for it once, the first time they answer on a device. 🔢 A PIN they choose Nothing to set up and no personal data. The student sets a 4–8 digit PIN the first time they pick their name, and needs it after that. The gap is that first claim — whoever gets there first owns the name — which you can see and clear in seconds. 🎟️ Codes you issue PollSlide generates a code per student and gives you a printable sheet to cut up and hand out. Nobody can claim a name they weren't given a code for, and still no personal data is stored. Codes avoid 0/O, 1/I and 5/S, and can't spell a word in front of a class. ✉️ Emailed codes The same code, sent to the student's school address — the strongest link to a real person. It's the only method that stores personal data, so it asks you to confirm your school has the right to use those addresses before switching on. Forgotten PIN? Reset it yourself from the class's…

topics.title: 🔁 Second attempts
topics.text: By default one answer is final. For a quiz you're using to find out who understood something, you can let students try again — and decide which try counts. Open the deck's ⋯ menu and choose 🔁 Retakes: off . Pick how many tries: 2 , 3 or 5 . Pick which attempt is graded — best , last or first . Students who've answered now see what they said, how many tries are left, and which attempt counts. 🏅 Best attempt The usual choice. The point of a retake is to let someone show they've got it now, and a later worse answer never pulls their grade back down. 🕐 Last attempt When the most recent answer is where their understanding actually stands — a revision round, or a set they're working through repeatedly. 1️⃣ First attempt The retake is recorded for you to look at, but the original is what's graded. Students are told this before they try again, so nobody wastes a go on a promise the deck won't keep. Every attempt is kept , whichever one you grade. In Reports an answer that came from a later try is marked 2nd try , so you can see who needed a second look at what. Not offered on polls. topics.title: 🎓 Gradebook export
topics.text: One row per student, one column per question, a score on the end — the shape your gradebook already has, and the shape Google Classroom and Canvas import. Open Reports . Choose one presentation in the filter — a gradebook is one deck's marks. Press 🎓 Gradebook . The file downloads, and PollSlide tells you what it contains and anything it left out. Import it into Classroom or Canvas, or open it in Excel, Numbers or Sheets. ⬜ A blank is not a zero A student who never answered and a student who answered wrongly are different facts. Missing answers stay blank and don't count against anyone; a wrong answer is a 0. The Answered column shows the difference at a glance. 🧮 Only what's actually graded A reflection prompt with no correct answer isn't part of a grade, so it doesn't become a column of blanks you'd have to delete. You're told how many were left out and why. ⤓ Two different exports ⤓ Answers gives you every response, one row each — for reading what people actually said. 🎓 Gradebook gives you the marks. Both are plain CSV that opens anywhere. Assign the deck to a class first. Without one, students are matched on the name they typed, so a stray spelling becomes a second row.…

topics.title: 👁 Know if someone leaves the screen
topics.text: For a graded quiz or a study set, you can be told when a student switches away from PollSlide — and they're told too, the moment it happens. Open the deck's ⋯ menu and choose 👁 Screen-leaving: not tracked to switch it on. Anyone answering now sees a short message on their own screen if they leave: “You left the screen — your teacher will see this.” Their answer records how many times they left that question, and for how long. It's counted per question , so you can see which one they left on — not just that they left at some point. Turn it off from the same menu. It's off by default on every deck. 🔓 It cannot lock their screen No website can. A browser has no way to stop someone switching apps or opening another tab — that needs a managed device, like a school MDM or a locked-down exam browser. Anything claiming otherwise in a normal browser isn't telling you the truth. 📣 They're told, not caught The on-screen message is the point. A student who knows it's being recorded can choose differently; one who finds out afterwards has just been trapped. That's why there's no silent mode. 🙈 It can't see what they switched to Only that PollSlide stopped being the front window, and for…

topics.text: Start free, upgrade only when you need more. One plan covers the whole suite — polls, surveys, quizzes and study sets. 🆓 Free Keep a few presentations, host small audiences, and get a monthly Polly AI allowance. For regular presenters, teachers and creators. 👥 Team Everything in Pro plus a shared workspace, member seats and centralised billing. topics.title: 👥 Teams & workspaces
topics.text: A Team plan puts everyone in your group on the same plan, on one bill. ▶ Set up your team in 2 minutes: invite people, roles, seats and billing. The person who buys the Team plan is the team's owner. Team admin opens by itself at their first sign-in, and is always in the avatar menu at the top right. Invite people by email as a member or an admin. They join automatically the next time they sign in with that address, on the team's plan. Admins can invite and remove people. Only the owner can turn an admin back into a member. Members can leave on their own at any time. One bill covers every seat. If the team plan ends, members keep all their work and go back to the Free plan. Seats: Team Small has 5 seats and Team Large has 25, including the owner. A pending invite holds a seat until it is accepted or revoked. Need more? Move up a tier, or email help@pollslide.com. Chapters and the written steps are on the team setup page.

topics.title: 🔒 Your data & privacy
topics.text: Your presentations and responses are yours. Here's how PollSlide handles them. 📥 Export any time Download every response as CSV from the Report screen. Your data is never locked in. 🗑️ Delete on request Remove a session, or your whole account and all its data, from your account settings — permanently. 🙈 No audience tracking Participants just scan and answer — no app, no account, no advertising trackers. 🖥️ Local screen reading The Mac Companion reads your screen only to spot the QR code. Nothing is recorded, saved, or sent. Full details are in our Privacy Policy , Terms of Service , and Trust & Safety pages. Questions about your data? Email help@pollslide.com .

topics.title: The companion isn't popping up on my QR slide
topics.text: Check three things: the app is in your Applications folder (not Downloads or the disk image); Screen Recording is ON for PollSlide Companion and you quit and reopened the app afterwards; and the menu reads “■ Stop Auto-Show (QR detect)” . If it reads “▶ Start Auto-Show (QR detect)” , click it. Make sure you're on the latest version from pollslide.com/download .

topics.title: My audience can't join or results aren't updating
topics.text: PollSlide needs an internet connection on both your device and your audience's. Check you're online, then have them re-scan the QR or go to pollslide.com/join and enter the code. Refresh the presenter page if a session looks stuck.

topics.title: The QR code won't scan
topics.text: Make it bigger on your slide and keep good contrast (dark on light). Most phone cameras scan automatically — if not, any QR app works, or use the pollslide.com/join + code option instead.

topics.title: Polly AI is slow or didn't generate
topics.text: Try again — the first request after a while can be slower. If you've hit your monthly Polly allowance, you'll be told; you can still add questions by hand or upgrade for more. See Plans & billing .

topics.title: The results window opened on the wrong screen
topics.text: Drag it by its top bar onto the display your slides are on — it stays there for the rest of your talk. With a projector or second display, always do a quick dry run first so you can position it once.

topics.title: The window covers the QR
topics.text: Your audience can't scan a QR the window is sitting on. Drag the window by its top bar, or move the QR to a corner of the slide — and test before you present.

topics.title: My study streak reset even though I studied
topics.text: The streak counts calendar days and only banks when you finish a session, so closing the tab halfway through won't count. It's also per-device (it lives in that browser), so studying on your phone and laptop keeps two separate streaks. Note it's now a single streak across all your sets — studying any set keeps it alive.

topics.title: PollSlide for Keynote — live polls without leaving Present mode
topics.text: Turn any Keynote slide into a live poll, quiz or Q&A your audience answers on their own phone. No plugin, nothing for anyone in the room to install — and a free Mac companion app floats the results right on top of your slideshow. If you've searched for a "Keynote plugin" for live polling, here's the honest answer: it doesn't exist — not from PollSlide, and not from anyone else. Apple doesn't publish a public add-in API for Keynote the way Microsoft does for PowerPoint or Google does for Slides, so no third-party tool can install itself inside the app. What actually works, and what presenters already use today, is simpler than a plugin: put a QR code on the slide. Why there's no "Keynote plugin" — and why that's fine Keynote is Mac-only and, unlike PowerPoint or Google Slides, has never opened itself up to third-party add-ins. So instead of promising an integration that can't be built, PollSlide treats every slide the same way Keynote already treats an image: something you paste in. A live poll becomes a picture — a QR code — sitting on your slide exactly where you put it. Your audience scans it, answers on their own phone, and you keep presenting from Keynote the entire time. The real, shipped setup for Keynote is two things: a QR code pasted onto your slide, and — optionally — a free menu-bar app that floats live results over whatever you're presenting. Copy a QR code out of PollSlide, paste it onto any slide right there in the browser, and present as normal — your audience scans it and answers on their own phone. Why there's no "Insert Poll" button — and why that's fine Google doesn't build live polling into Slides, and most third-party add-ons only work inside the Slides editor itself, not on the big screen once you hit Present. PollSlide sidesteps the whole question: a live poll, quiz or survey question just becomes a small QR image that you paste onto a slide like a picture. Google Slides already knows how to show a picture. That's the entire integration. It's the same method PollSlide uses for Keynote and PowerPoint, because it's the one method that's guaranteed to keep working no matter which slide tool you're standing in front of a room with.
